The Impact

The Numbers. The People. The Change.

The numbers matter because the people behind them mattered first.

I'm Possible has directly supported over 100 young people since its founding. Each one a person who had previously been unable to speak - who found in an I'm Possible conversation the first space in which they felt safe enough to try. Several of those conversations were not merely helpful. They were life-saving. Moments where a peer-to-peer connection became the difference between a young person reaching the edge and finding a way back from it.

These are not metrics. They are people. The numbers are recorded because accountability matters and because the case for peer-led mental health support needs evidence. But the reason I'm Possible exists is not the number. It is the person behind it.

The Jack Petchey Achievement Award.

In 2024, Abishek won the Jack Petchey Achievement Award - one of the UK's most prestigious youth honours - by a landslide. He received hundreds of votes from peers, teachers, and heads of year across nearly 800 eligible students at Queen Elizabeth's School: a selection rate of just 0.8%. He was not recognised for academic achievement. He was recognised for the tangible, witnessed impact of I'm Possible on the mental health and lives of the students around him.

The £300 grant that accompanies the award was directed entirely back into school mental health facilities and the expansion of the peer mentorship scheme. Not because it was required. Because the recognition was never the point. The work is the point.

"The Jack Petchey Foundation has invested over £140 million in young people across London and Essex. Its Achievement Award is not selected by panels or institutions - it is selected by the community itself. By peers. By the people who witnessed the impact first-hand."

Recognition beyond the school.

I'm Possible and its founder have been recognised at the highest levels of national and international public life. Abishek was one of only 20 young changemakers globally invited to the Transforming Global Education Summit at UN ECOSOC Headquarters in New York in 2026. He was invited by the United Nations Secretariat to the Geneva Sustainable Management Workshop at the Palais des Nations. He presented MenTomorrow's research and policy proposals at the House of Lords. His work was covered by the Guardian, featured on S4C, and broadcast on BBC News.

These recognitions are not listed for prestige. They are listed because they constitute external, independent validation that the problem I'm Possible addresses is real, that the approach is credible, and that the young person leading it is someone the world's most credible institutions trust enough to invite into their rooms.

UN ECOSOC - New York

1 of 20 young changemakers globally invited to the Transforming Global Education Summit at UN ECOSOC Headquarters in New York, 2026. Selected by Executive Chairman Sergio A. Fernandez de Cordova in recognition of leadership in youth empowerment and education reform.

UN Geneva - Palais des Nations

Invited by the United Nations Secretariat to the Geneva Sustainable Management Workshop at the United Nations Office in Geneva on 22 May 2026, as part of the Global Impact Project to Refinance International Geneva.

S4C & BBC News

Featured contributor in a two-part current affairs documentary for S4C and BBC News, investigating manosphere radicalisation. Invited by Jet TV following coverage in the Guardian and previous television appearances.

Aspire Fellowship - NIH & Harvard

Sole recipient of a full-ride $3,000 Aspire Scholarship from 20,000 global applicants. Conducting two clinical research studies on youth mental health governance and Haeven - an AI-powered anxiety regulation device - under Dr. Shelton Lo, Postdoctoral Fellow at NIH, PhD Harvard.

What impact looks like going forward.

By September 2027, I'm Possible aims to have trained 14 NHS-supervised Mental Health Ambassadors across every year group at QE, published three editions of the I'm Possible Magazine, completed the first school-wide annual mental health survey, presented the first Student Mental Health Manifesto to school leadership, and expanded to at least one further secondary school in the NLFT CAMHS catchment area. The long-term vision is every school in Barnet, Enfield, and Haringey - 323,000+ young people.

Impact, for I'm Possible, is not a number on a dashboard. It is the student who finds the courage to speak. The ambassador who knows what to do. The school that cannot ignore the evidence placed in front of it. The borough that builds something that lasts.
